site/src/data/thesis-analyst-live-comparisons.ts:929:          text: "Forecast Australia May 2026 unemployment first print",
site/src/data/thesis-analyst-live-comparisons.ts:933:          text: "The resolver is the ABS Labour Force, Australia May 2026 release, using the seasonally adjusted national unemployment rate on the first official print. The ABS publication page says the May 2026 release is scheduled for 25/06/2026 at 11:30am AEST, so the resolution date is 2026-06-25.",
site/src/data/thesis-analyst-live-comparisons.ts:947:            "Fetched April 2026 seasonally adjusted unemployment rate 4.5%, up 0.2 ppt; unemployed people 692,500; employment decreased by 18,600 to 14,737,400; participation rate 66.7%.",
site/src/data/thesis-analyst-live-comparisons.ts:954:            "Fetched seasonally adjusted unemployment rates: January 2026 4.1%, February 2026 4.3%, March 2026 4.3%; February participation 66.9%, March participation 66.8%.",
site/src/data/thesis-analyst-live-comparisons.ts:961:            "Fetched April 2026 trend unemployment rate 4.3%, trend unemployed people 669,500, seasonally adjusted unemployed people 692,500, and May 2026 survey reference weeks 3 May 2026 to 16 May 2026.",
site/src/data/thesis-analyst-live-comparisons.ts:965:          text: "Base-rate/reference-class: adjacent-month Australian unemployment prints usually move by 0.0 to 0.2 percentage points at one-decimal precision outside shocks. The latest four seasonally adjusted prints, 4.1, 4.3, 4.3, and 4.5, imply a level around the mid-4s, while the April trend estimate of 4.3 suggests not all of the April spike should be extrapolated.",
site/src/data/thesis-analyst-live-comparisons.ts:969:          text: "Counter-consideration: April could mark genuine labour-market weakening, with employment down 18,600 and unemployed people up 33,000, so a further increase to 4.6 or 4.7 is plausible. Against that, hours worked rose 16 million and participation slipped to 66.7%, so the unemployment rate may stabilize rather than keep rising immediately.",
site/src/data/thesis-analyst-live-comparisons.ts:1359:        "April unemployment rate rose to 6.9 percent",
site/src/data/thesis-analyst-live-comparisons.ts:1360:        "April unemployment increased by 51000 people",
site/src/data/thesis-analyst-live-comparisons.ts:1494:            "Employment was 21034000 in April 2026, down 0.1% or 18000; the unemployment rate was 6.9%, up 0.2 percentage points; unemployment increased by 51000 or 3.4%.",
site/src/data/thesis-analyst-live-comparisons.ts:1502:          text: "Implied February count is 548000 - 2300 = 545700; implied January count is 545700 + 8700 = 554400. I start at 548000 and add roughly 8000 for April because unemployment rose by 51000 and the EI count usually moves less than one-for-one and with administrative lag. Point = 548000 + 8000 = 556000. An 80% interval of 535000 to 580000 covers a decline back below February through a return near the November 2025 peak of 569000 plus upside noise.",
site/src/data/thesis-analyst-live-comparisons.ts:1506:          text: "Counter-consideration: the April LFS rise in unemployment partly reflected more people searching for work, not only layoffs, and EI eligibility is limited to insured job losses. That argues against translating the full 51000 unemployment increase into EI beneficiaries.",
site/src/data/thesis-analyst-live-comparisons.ts:2647:          text: "Counter-consideration: an outcome near 5.7 percent or lower could happen if wage growth is broad, housing and food burdens ease, and refundable-credit take-up is near-complete. An outcome near 12.0 percent or higher could happen if unemployment rises, rent or medical out-of-pocket costs lift SPM needs, or filing and implementation frictions limit receipt among low-income families.",

site/src/data/thesis-analyst-live-comparisons.ts:4930:            "Fetched calendar note that the release calendar uses Europe/Luxembourg time zone and the April unemployment release shows Next release: 2 July 2026.",
site/src/data/thesis-analyst-live-comparisons.ts:4934:          text: "Base rate/reference class: monthly euro area unemployment rates usually move slowly at one-decimal precision; the last five official points shown for the euro area are 6.3, 6.3, 6.4, 6.3, and 6.3, making 6.3 the modal and median recent print.",
site/src/data/thesis-analyst-live-comparisons.ts:4942:          text: "Counter-consideration: Q1 GDP contraction of 0.2%, weaker retail trade, and higher May inflation at 3.2% could weaken demand and push unemployment up. site/src/data/thesis-analyst-live-comparisons.ts:4946:          text: "Use recent monthly persistence as the anchor: median(6.3, 6.3, 6.4, 6.3, 6.3) = 6.3. site/src/data/thesis-analyst-live-comparisons.ts:8048:          text: "Forecast Japan May 2026 first-print unemployment rate",
site/src/data/thesis-analyst-live-comparisons.ts:8052:          text: "The resolver is the Statistics Bureau of Japan Labour Force Survey Basic Tabulation complete unemployment rate, seasonally adjusted, for May 2026, taken from the first official monthly release and rounded as the agency publishes it to one decimal percentage point.",
site/src/data/thesis-analyst-live-comparisons.ts:8070:          text: "Base-rate/reference-class anchor: before using the April movement as inside-view evidence, the official-source reference class points to a low-volatility unemployment-rate range around 2.5 to 2.7 percent. The 2024 and 2025 annual rates were both 2.5 percent, so the outside-view prior is 2.5 percent with a short-run range centered near 2.6 percent.",
site/src/data/thesis-analyst-live-comparisons.ts:8081:            "Latest official page is the 2026 April release, published 2026-05-29, with seasonally adjusted complete unemployment rate 2.5%, down 0.2 percentage point from the prior month.",
site/src/data/thesis-analyst-live-comparisons.ts:8088:            "The April 2026 PDF reports employed persons 68.60 million, up 0.64 million year over year; unemployed persons 1.93 million, up 0.05 million year over year; labor force 70.53 million, up 0.69 million year over year; seasonally adjusted unemployment rate 2.5%.",
site/src/data/thesis-analyst-live-comparisons.ts:8128:        "May payroll growth of 172,000 and unchanged 4.3 percent unemployment are public pre-release evidence against a sharp demand drop",
site/src/data/thesis-analyst-live-comparisons.ts:8539:            "BLS reported May 2026 nonfarm payroll employment increased by 172,000, unemployment was 4.3 percent, April payroll growth was revised to 179,000, and March was revised to 214,000.",
site/src/data/thesis-analyst-live-comparisons.ts:8551:          text: "Level and momentum effects point in opposite directions. April's 7.618 million level is high relative to January through March, but May payrolls were solid and unemployment was unchanged, so I expect only a partial reversal of the April jump rather than a fall back to the March trough.",
site/src/data/thesis-analyst-live-comparisons.ts:8591:        "May payroll growth was solid at 172,000 and unemployment held at 4.3 percent",
site/src/data/thesis-analyst-live-comparisons.ts:8725:            "BLS reported May 2026 payroll employment +172,000, unemployment rate 4.3 percent, April payroll revision to +179,000, and March payroll revision to +214,000.",
site/src/data/thesis-analyst-live-comparisons.ts:8733:          text: "The upside case is that solid May payroll growth and stable unemployment mean labor demand remained firm, so April's 7,618 thousand could persist into May.",
site/src/data/thesis-analyst-live-comparisons.ts:17963:        "unemployment steady at 4.3 percent",
site/src/data/thesis-analyst-live-comparisons.ts:18082:            "BLS reported total nonfarm payroll employment increased by 172,000 in May 2026 and unemployment was 4.3 percent.",
site/src/data/thesis-analyst-live-comparisons.ts:18104:          text: "Upside case: upward revisions and a steady 4.3 percent unemployment rate suggest the labor market had more momentum than April's initial print implied, and May sector gains in leisure and hospitality, local government, and health care could persist into June.",
site/src/data/thesis-analyst-live-comparisons.ts:18266:          call: "Checked the latest official DOL unemployment insurance weekly claims release for layoff pressure near the survey month.",
site/src/data/thesis-analyst-live-comparisons.ts:18268:            "DOL reported initial claims of 226,000 for the week ending Jun. 13, 2026, down 4,000 from the revised 230,000 prior week; the 4-week moving average was 223,250, up 4,000; insured unemployment was 1,810,000 for the week ending Jun. 6.",
site/src/data/thesis-analyst-live-comparisons.ts:18748:            "Fetched January 2026 unemployment rate 4.3 percent, December 2025 unemployment rate 4.4 percent, January 2026 payroll gain 130000, and revised 2025 payroll gain 181000.",
site/src/data/thesis-analyst-live-comparisons.ts:18760:          text: "Policy mechanism: because the official measure is pretax cash income, many 2025 changes to taxes, credits, SNAP, medical costs, and housing costs matter less directly than they would for the SPM. Cash earnings, Social Security cash income, unemployment, and official poverty-threshold changes are the main channels for this resolver.",

site/src/data/thesis-analyst-live-comparisons.ts:22496:          text: "The resolver is the ONS Labour Force Survey unemployment rate for people aged 16 and over, seasonally adjusted, for the July to September 2026 rolling three-month period. The target is the first one-decimal print in the November 2026 UK Labour Market or Employment in the UK release.",
site/src/data/thesis-analyst-live-comparisons.ts:22514:          call: "Opened ONS time-series page MGSX for the unemployment rate aged 16 and over, seasonally adjusted.",
site/src/data/thesis-analyst-live-comparisons.ts:22523:            "Fetched latest LFS unemployment rate for February to April 2026 = 4.9%, up 0.3 percentage points on the year and down 0.3 percentage points on the latest quarter; PAYE employees fell 103,000 over the year and 31,000 on the quarter for February to April 2026; March to May 2026 vacancies fell 19,000 to 707,000.",
site/src/data/thesis-analyst-live-comparisons.ts:22530:            "Fetched February to April 2026 unemployment level 1.764 million, unemployment-rate sampling variability \u00b10.3 percentage points, quarterly change -0.3 percentage points, annual change +0.3 percentage points, and achieved LFS sample 80,078 individuals in January to March 2026.",
site/src/data/thesis-analyst-live-comparisons.ts:22542:          text: "Policy and measurement mechanism: the target is a household-survey unemployment rate, not a claimant-count or payroll series. Soft PAYE and vacancies tend to lift unemployment with a lag, but seasonal-adjustment review and LFS sampling variability can move the first print by several tenths without a true labour-market break.",
site/src/data/thesis-analyst-live-comparisons.ts:22546:          text: "Counter-consideration: the print could come below 4.5 if the February-April quarterly fall marks a genuine re-tightening in labour demand or if inactivity absorbs job losses. It could exceed 5.8 if payroll weakness broadens into layoffs, vacancies keep falling, and LFS volatility prints another sharp unemployment increase.",
site/src/data/thesis-analyst-live-comparisons.ts:22550:          text: "Point calculation: start with a 5.0 percent outside-view anchor from recent quarterly MGSX values, blend in the latest 4.9 percent February-April level, then add about 0.15 percentage points for weak PAYE employment and vacancies over the five-month release horizon: 0.45*5.0 + 0.35*4.9 + 0.20*5.3 = 5.025, rounded and judgmentally tilted to 5.1 because labour-demand indicators are soft. For the 80% interval, the recent rolling MGSX sequence moved within 4.9 to 5.2 percent and the latest bulletin gives about \u00b10.3 percentage-point sampling variability, so I start near \u00b10.5 around the point and widen the upper side for lagged unemployment risk, giving 4.5 to 5.8.",
